subject: biology
title: Gene Regulation & Epigenetics Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll regulate genes — from the lac operon in bacteria to epigenetic marks in eukaryotes.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology Gene Expression — lac operon, transcription factors, DNA methylation and histone modification.
final_note: You learned how the lac operon switches on with lactose, how transcription factors control eukaryote genes, and how DNA methylation and histone acetylation alter expression without changing the DNA sequence.

concepts.def: Cluster of genes with a single promoter — prokaryotic gene control unit
E. coli genes for lactose metabolism — switched on only when lactose present
Protein binding DNA to switch genes on/off in eukaryotes
Adding -CH3 to cytosine — usually silences genes
Adding acetyl groups to histones — loosens DNA, increases expression
Heritable changes in expression without changes in DNA sequence

walkthroughs.body_html:
E. coli only makes lactose-digesting enzymes when lactose is around.

Structure: promoter — operator — structural genes (lacZ, lacY, lacA).

No lactose: a repressor protein binds the operator → blocks RNA polymerase → genes off.

Lactose present: lactose binds the repressor → repressor changes shape → falls off operator → RNA polymerase transcribes the genes → enzymes made.

Eukaryotic regulation is more elaborate. Transcription factors are proteins that bind specific DNA sequences (promoters or enhancers).

- Activators recruit RNA polymerase II
- Repressors block it

Example: oestrogen binds a receptor in cytoplasm → complex enters nucleus → acts as transcription factor → switches on target genes.

DNA sequence is the same in every cell — so why are liver and brain cells so different? Epigenetics.

DNA methylation — methyl groups added to cytosine in CpG islands → gene silenced.

Histone modification — acetylation loosens DNA from histones → easier to transcribe; deacetylation tightens it → silenced.

Marks can be inherited and influenced by environment — diet, stress, smoking.
